hypotheses.rationale: flashLoan asserts convertToShares(totalSupply)==balanceBefore; a direct token transfer into the vault breaks the ERC4626 assets==shares invariant, permanently reverting all flash loans.

flashLoan uses arbitrary receiver and charges a fixed fee; an attacker can repeatedly force loans on a victim receiver draining its WETH balance via fees, and the meta-tx forwarder allows withdrawing pool funds on behalf of others.
flashLoan uses transferFrom from the receiver with arbitrary from, but the deeper risk is that the governance token loan grants voting power enabling drainage via emergencyExit.

proxyCreated pays out tokens to beneficiary-owned Safes created via the factory; an attacker can craft the initializer to set a malicious module/owner and redirect the registry's payout to drain funds.
xSender is set from l2Sender then reset to 0xBADBEEF; combined with weak proof validation, an attacker can finalize arbitrary withdrawals impersonating the authorized L2 sender.
execute performs delegatecall to a caller-controlled target/data, allowing arbitrary code execution in the vault's storage context if reachable by an unprivileged caller.
flashLoan executes an arbitrary call on an attacker-controlled target with arbitrary data, so the attacker can make the pool approve() the attacker for the full token balance and then drain it.
flashLoan only checks ETH balance after the callback; attacker can deposit the borrowed funds back via deposit() satisfying the balance check, then withdraw() to drain the pool.
The governance token is flash-loanable; borrowing enough tokens grants temporary voting power to queue a malicious proposal calling emergencyExit, draining the pool after the timelock.
emergencyExit transfers all tokens to an arbitrary receiver and is gated only by governance; a flash-loan-powered governance proposal lets an attacker schedule and execute it to drain the pool.
claimRewards marks claims as consumed only per-batch; repeating the same valid claim within a single call array lets an attacker claim the same reward multiple times and drain the distributor.
msg.value is validated once per NFT inside a loop, so a single payment covering the highest price can buy multiple NFTs, and the proceeds are paid to the buyer, netting the attacker funds.
Collateral value uses Curve LP get_virtual_price via _getLPTokenPrice, which can be manipulated with flash-loaned liquidity/reentrancy to force liquidations and seize collateral cheaply.
borrow computes required WETH collateral from a Uniswap V2 spot reserve ratio, which an attacker can skew via a large swap to borrow tokens for near-zero collateral and drain the pool.
borrow derives collateral from a Uniswap V3 TWAP over a short window; manipulating the pool tick and advancing time lets the attacker depress the quote and borrow tokens cheaply.

drop's can() authorization check can halt-return 0 and is misread as success, plus the unchecked transfer payout, letting an attacker deploy wallets and claim the gem reward without proper validation.
Withdrawal execution relies on L1Gateway's replayable/forgeable message verification (xSender overwrite finding); an attacker can submit a crafted withdrawal to transfer bridge tokens to themselves.
Rounding with mulDivUp/mulDivDown between fill and cancel/_closeOffer plus rate conversion mismatches can let a buyer reclaim more payment tokens than paid, netting funds from the marketplace.

execute runs the operation calls before checking it was scheduled, allowing an attacker to batch calls that grant themselves PROPOSER_ROLE and schedule the same operation, bypassing the timelock to take over the vault.
Upgrade authorization is onlyOwner (the timelock); once the timelock execute flaw grants control, the attacker can upgrade the vault to an implementation that sweeps all funds.
